p2: evidence shortened to the key clause; name kept as fragment '[...]ka', with a note that 'śrīma' may be the honorific śrīmat- rather than part of the name
date.ce_approx: changed from the single year 1090 to the reign range c. 1085–1098
notes: added the unclear 'śrīmatparākhyena' phrase and the lacunae in the dating verse

persons.evidence: nepāladeśaṃ samupāgatena kāṣṭhābhidhe maṃḍape saṃsthitena | svaśiṣyavarggasya viśodhanāya … śrīma..................kenāpi saṃlekhi ca paṃḍitena

purpose: for correcting the copies of his own disciples (svaśiṣyavarggasya viśodhanāya) and for the benefit of others (paropakārāya)
notes: The year and tithi are lost in a lacuna. Only the bright fortnight of Āśvina and the reign of Harṣadeva survive, so the CE date can only be placed within his reign (c. 1085–1098). This fits the catalogue's 'early 12th century' only loosely; late 11th century is more likely. The scribe's name is broken: 'śrīma…ka'. 'Śrīma' may be the honorific śrīmat- rather than part of the name. The scribe is described as having come to Nepal and as living at Kāṣṭhamaṇḍapa, so he was probably a foreign paṇḍita. 'svayaṃ … uptatam' is probably a corruption of 'udyatam'. The phrase 'śrīmatparākhyena vidhī (not clear)' in the verse giving the extent (2,500 ślokas) is unclear. It may name someone connected with the text, possibly its author, but it is too damaged to identify, so no one was extracted from it.
